messages:
Maya (CS): Heads up — SaffronLabs renewal in ~6w. Usage down ~48% last 30d and they reported intermittent `500` spikes on their staging namespace. Procurement has asked for a cost/latency plan. Need triage + a procurement-friendly summary. :warning:
Jon (Solutions): On it. Do we have endpoint-level logs?
Maya (CS): They called out /v1/generation and /v1/embeddings. Errors cluster 11:00-12:00 PDT. Pasted two sample lines from their support bundle:
```
2026-03-17T18:58:12Z - 500 - kv_cache_miss - latency=1.9s
2026-03-17T19:01:03Z - 502 - batch_timeout - batch_size=1
```
Ari (Eng): Sounds like batching/backpressure + small bursty traffic -> cold KV cache. Can we repro with their request pattern?
Maya (CS): Uploaded a few traces to our customer s3: https://s3.company/saffron/traces-03-17
Luis (Sales): FYI procurement may be running a competitive eval with NimbusAI. They asked for a perf report + cost estimate. Recommend we push operational mitigations first rather than a straight discount. :eyes:
Jon (Solutions): Proposed immediate play: 1) confirm SDK + streaming usage; 2) offer temporary routing to dedicated pool during peak; 3) publish short batching/timeout guide for small callers. I can draft an exec summary.
Maya (CS): Note: their Head of ML left last week; new procurement contact is Karen M. — less technical. Need an exec-level summary for procurement + a concise ops checklist for their ML lead.
Ari (Eng): I'll run a load sweep on staging to reproduce KV thrash + measure cold-starts. ETA ~4h. Short-term fix idea: reduce `max_wait_ms` to 20ms for their tenant and increase per-request concurrency to avoid single-request timeouts.
Luis (Sales): I'll check procurement's eval criteria and whether they expect price concessions. Prefer operational concessions (trial of dedicated routing) rather than discounting renewal.
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy 2026-03-18T03:00 UTC (rollback window 1h). Tagging @Ari (Eng).
Ari (Eng): Noted — will coordinate to ensure canary excludes Saffron's dedicated pool.
Maya (CS): Action items: Jon - draft procurement-friendly exec summary (owner: Jon) due EOD; Ari - run repro + share logs + quick config change (owner: Ari) due in 4h; Luis - confirm procurement ask and competitive status (owner: Luis) due EOD; Maya - schedule 30m call with customer (owner: Maya) tomorrow.
Luis (Sales): I'll also ask if they have a formal RFP or benchmarking sheet for the eval.
Jon (Solutions): Drafting now; will include cost delta for dedicated vs hosted, expected latency gains, and recommended temporary routing plan.
Maya (CS): They also mentioned "occasional truncated responses" — could be related. If anyone gets prompt examples, add them to the doc.
Ari (Eng): If responses are truncated, could be tokenization/sequence-length mismatch or early stream termination. Send examples and I'll check server-side logs.
Maya (CS): Pulling prompt examples from ticket and will paste here once I have them.
Luis (Sales): :thumbsup: Strong preference to sell reliability solution (short-term dedicated routing + config) rather than price cut.
Jon (Solutions): Uploaded first draft: https://docs.company/saffron/procurement-exec-summary-draft — PTAL @Maya (CS) @Luis (Sales)
Maya (CS): Reviewed, left comments on the SLA bullets. Suggest adding a "fallback model variant" line and a 2-week stabilization offer instead of discount.
Jon (Solutions): Added fallback-variant note and a simple rollback + monitoring playbook.
Maya (CS): Scheduling customer call: tomorrow 10:30 PDT. Invite sent to Karen M., Saffron PM, and our reps.
Luis (Sales): I'll join the call and push to get competitive evaluation details.
Ari (Eng): If we confirm batching/backpressure, I can push the temporary `max_wait_ms` change ASAP and monitor.
Maya (CS): If procurement asks for a formal SLA, escalate to legal for the standard SLA template.
Luis (Sales): Will flag legal if needed.
Maya (CS): Thanks team — will update after the call. :pray:
